issues.failure_explanation: The first integrand compares D_x v~^theta evaluated at [Phi_t^theta]^{-1}(x) with D_x u^mu evaluated at the different point [Phi_t^mu]^{-1}(x). It is then bounded by sup_x ||D_x(v~_t - u_t)(x)||, which only controls the difference at a common point. The missing term D_x u^mu([Phi_t^theta]^{-1}(x)) - D_x u^mu([Phi_t^mu]^{-1}(x)) requires Lipschitz continuity of D_x u^mu (a C^2 bound on u^mu) times the C^0 flow difference, which is not invoked.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and subtract D_x u^mu([Phi_t^theta]^{-1}(x),1-t), bound the extra term by ||u^mu||_{C^2} times the Gronwall estimate for ||[Phi_t^theta]^{-1}(x) - [Phi_t^mu]^{-1}(x)||, using the cited uniform C^k (k>=3) bound on u^mu (via u^mu ⊘ eta_d); constants then also depend on k.
issues.overall_effect: The bound (kl_target_approx_thm) KL <= c ||v~ - u||_{C^1} is not established as written; the model-error control used in the main theorem inherits the gap.
issues.title: Jacobians of the two vector fields compared at different base points in the model-error proof
issues.why_classification: A short local argument using already-cited ingredients (uniform C^k bound on u^mu, Gronwall) closes the gap; the conclusion and rate in K survive with adjusted constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, the determinant sensitivity estimate from~\cite[Cor.~2.14]{ipsen2008} yields

issues.failure_explanation: The cited determinant perturbation bound controls |det(A+E) - det A| (or its relative version with the factor ||A^{-1}||), not a difference of logarithms. The inequality |log|det A| - log|det B|| <= sum_k C(d,k) 2^k ||A-B||^k is false in general: for d=1, A=0.01, B=0.02 the left side is log 2 while the right side is 0.02. Passing from determinants to their logarithms requires a lower bound on |det D_x[Phi^theta]^{-1}(x)| (available only as exp(-d sqrt d ||v~||_{C^1})-type quantities, not 1/2), and the unexplained factor 2^k does not supply it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step by the Liouville representation log|det D_x[Phi^theta]^{-1}(x)| = -∫_0^1 div v~^theta(y(t),1-t) dt (used already in (eq:liouville_log_det)) and bound differences of the divergence integrals via C^1/C^{1,1} bounds and Gronwall, or apply the Ipsen–Rehman relative bound together with an explicit lower determinant bound exp(-d sqrt d ||v~||_{C^1}); then recompute L-bar and D (still of the exp(poly(sqrt q Lip_1)) form).
issues.overall_effect: The Jacobian-determinant contributions in the model-error bound, the sub-Gaussian constant L-bar, and the McDiarmid constant D are unsupported as written; all downstream constants and the architecture schedule of the main theorem must be re-derived.
issues.title: False log-determinant perturbation inequality used in three proofs
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument exists and the results survive in comparable form, but three proofs and the explicit constants feeding Remarks rmk:main_constant_L/rmk:main_constant_D and the L_n, W_n schedule must be re-derived.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:lip_constants gives Lipschitz continuity in theta at a fixed point (x,t). Here the two Jacobians are evaluated at different spatial points [Phi_t^theta]^{-1}(x) and [Phi_t^{theta'}]^{-1}(x), so the displayed inequality does not follow. Closing the gap needs a uniform Lipschitz (in x) bound for D_x v~^theta over the ReQU hypothesis class (a C^{1,1} bound), which the paper never establishes, combined with the flow-difference estimate (subg_est_1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a lemma bounding the spatial Lipschitz constant of D_x(v^theta ⊗ eta_d) uniformly over [-1,1]^q for ReQU networks (ReQU is C^{1,1}) in terms of L, W, d; insert the cross term via the flow difference (subg_est_1); recompute L-bar and verify that Remark rmk:main_constant_L's growth form (hence the choice of L_n, W_n) still holds.
issues.overall_effect: The Lipschitz-in-theta increment bound |Z_theta - Z_theta'| <= L-bar ||theta - theta'|| is unproven, so the Dudley bound, the concentration bound and the PAC argument rest on an unestablished constant.
issues.title: Sub-Gaussianity proof bounds Jacobian difference at different points by the parameter-Lipschitz constant
issues.why_classification: Requires a new contained lemma on second-order network bounds and re-derivation of the constants driving the architecture schedule; the result plausibly survives with the same structure.

issues.failure_explanation: Raising the preceding bound to the k-th power produces (Lip_1^Theta)^k ||theta-theta'||^k, but the factor (Lip_1^Theta)^k (Lip_1 >> 1) is omitted in (subg_est_2) and hence in the stated constant L-bar; the analogous step in thm:concentration_bound keeps it. The stated L-bar is therefore not a valid Lipschitz constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor (Lip_1^Theta)^d into (subg_est_2) and into the definition of L-bar; Remark rmk:main_constant_L remains valid since Lip_1^d <= exp(d Lip_1).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit expression for L-bar in Lemma lem:sub_gaussian is too small; the growth form in Remark rmk:main_constant_L still absorbs the missing factor.
issues.title: Factor Lip_1^k dropped in the determinant term of the sub-Gaussian constant
issues.why_classification: Purely a constant correction that a routine recomputation fixes without affecting any downstream statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalization error is sup_theta |Z_{theta,n}|, but the proof equates its expectation with E sup_theta Z_{theta,n}, which is what the chaining bound controls. Passing from sup Z to sup |Z| requires E sup|Z| <= E|Z_{theta_0}| + E sup(Z_theta - Z_{theta_0}) + E sup(Z_{theta_0} - Z_theta), i.e. a factor 2 on the Dudley integral plus an additive term E|Z_{theta_0}| = O(sup_x|log f_{mu_theta_0}(x)|/sqrt n) that the stated bound 48 L W^2 L-bar/sqrt n does not account for.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound E sup|Z| by E|Z_{theta_0}| plus twice the Dudley integral, bound E|Z_{theta_0}| via the uniform bound on |log f_{mu_theta}| (from kappa, K and Corollary cor:c1_bound), and adjust the constant (still of the form const·L-bar-type/sqrt n).
issues.overall_effect: The numerical constant in Theorems thm:dudley and thm:concentration_bound and the threshold n_2 in the main proof are not justified as stated; the 1/sqrt n rate is unaffected.
issues.title: Dudley bound applied to sup Z instead of sup |Z|
issues.why_classification: A routine local correction changing only constants; rate and all downstream conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all $m \geq m(n)$, which is always possible because the function
provided also that the number of quadrature points $m \geq m(n^*)$ is sufficiently large.

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature error is controlled only through the worst-case bound ||Φ^θ||_{C^1} <= sqrt d exp(sqrt d sqrt q Lip_1^Θ(L_n,W_n)), which grows without bound as n→∞ because W_n, L_n→∞. Hence the threshold m(n) in (eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd) depends on n and increases with n. Setting m(ε,δ) := m(n(ε,δ)) makes the quadrature error bound hold only at n = n(ε,δ); for n > n(ε,δ) with m fixed at m(ε,δ) the bound ε/2 is not established. The statement (and definition (defn:pac_learnability)) requires independent thresholds valid for all n >= n(ε,δ) and all ℓ >= ℓ(ε,δ), which the proof does not deliver; no n-uniform C^1 bound on the ERM flow is available.

failure_location.quote: such that for all sample sizes $n,m \geq n(\varepsilon,\delta), m(\varepsilon,\delta)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement/definition to: for every ε,δ there exist n(ε,δ) and a nondecreasing function m(n) such that P(ε^total > ε) <= δ for all n >= n(ε,δ) and m >= m(n) (quadrature level adapted to n), or alternatively restrict to a fixed architecture for n large enough after which the model error is already below threshold and then quadrature thresholds are uniform.
issues.overall_effect: The PAC-learnability claim with independent sample-size and sparsity-level thresholds (defn:pac_learnability) is unsupported; only a version in which the quadrature level is coupled to the sample size (m >= m(n)) is proven.
issues.title: Quadrature threshold m(ε,δ) cannot be uniform in n because the C^1 bound on Φ^{θ̂_n} grows with the architecture
issues.why_classification: A central quantifier is weakened (coupled rather than independent thresholds), but a recognizably comparable consistency result along an adaptive schedule survives without new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The established decomposition (empirical_error_decomp) has 2ε_n^gen, but the main proof invokes it without the factor 2, so the event {ε^gen > ε²/(16||qoi||²)} should be {ε^gen > ε²/(32||qoi||²)}; the subsequent thresholds n_2 and the exponent ε^4/4096 are therefore not correctly derived.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the factor 2 and propagate the change through (eq:main_thm_model_error_bd), (main_thm_exp_gen_err_bd) and the final threshold (constants 16→32, 32→64, 4096→16384).
issues.overall_effect: Explicit constants in the sample-size threshold n(ε,δ) of the main theorem are off by fixed factors; the qualitative PAC conclusion is unaffected.
issues.title: Factor 2 on the generalization error dropped in the main proof's risk decomposition
issues.why_classification: Routine constant propagation; no statement beyond explicit numerical constants changes.
